newsitem.title: UK: Dlr choppy after spike above 120 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dlr choppy after spike above 120 yen.

text.p: The dollar reversed in early European trading after a brief spike above 120 yen amid a spate of contradictory comments out of Japan, traders said.
It made a long-awaited stab above a key level of 120 yen, buoyed by official comments out of Japan that a weak yen was not doing much damage to the economy.
These comments were taken by the market as a green light to carry the dollar higher, pushing it to 120.15, its highest in 47 months.
However, a later comment by an official from Japan's finance ministry (MOF) that an excessively weak yen was not welcome by Japan dragged the dollar lower.
Rumours that the Bank of Japan might have sold dollar/yen also capped the dollar's rise, traders said.
At 0830 GMT the dollar stood at 119.25 yen, down from 119.57 in late European trade on Thursday.
"The market is clearly nervous about the comments coming out of Japan, but it also wants to see the dollar go higher," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro.
Another comment, from a Japanese government spokesman that he is confident that the yen will not fall below the 120 yen level, served only to confuse the market further, dealers said.
Analysts said the dollar may be in for a slight correction after its latest run to above 120 yen.

However, few doubted that the dollar would strengthen more, saying that interest rate differentials between the United States and Japan and other economic fundamentals all pointed to a stronger dollar.
